subject: math
title: The Coordinate Plane: Ordered Pairs, Plotting Points and Real-World Graphs
seo_title: Grade 5 Coordinate Plane Worksheets: Ordered Pairs, Plotting Points in the First Quadrant (5.G.A.1-2)
standard_text: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis. Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 coordinate plane worksheets: read and plot ordered pairs in the first quadrant, points on the x-axis and y-axis, the origin, distance along a grid line, the 4th corner of a rectangle, and real-world maps and graphs. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: An ordered pair (x, y) is a set of directions from the origin: go right x, then up y.
key_sub: The x-coordinate always comes first, so (3, 7) and (7, 3) are different points. A point with x = 0 is on the y-axis, and a point with y = 0 is on the x-axis.
body_html:
What a coordinate grid is

A coordinate grid is made of two number lines that cross at 0. The x-axis goes across. The y-axis goes up. They meet at the origin, (0, 0).

An ordered pair (x, y) tells you how to get to a point from the origin: the first number says how far to go right, the second says how far to go up.

Example

A point is 6 units to the right of the origin and 2 units up. What are its coordinates?

Right 6 is the x-coordinate. Up 2 is the y-coordinate. Write x first.

Answer: (6, 2)

Order matters. (3, 5) and (5, 3) are different points.

Points on the axes

PointWhere it isWhy
(0, 4)on the y-axisx = 0: no move to the right
(5, 0)on the x-axisy = 0: no move up
(0, 0)the originno move at all

Distance along a grid line

If two points have the same x-coordinate, they are on the same up-and-down line. Subtract the y-coordinates. If they have the same y-coordinate, subtract the x-coordinates.

Example

How far is it from (1, 6) to (8, 6)?

Same y, so subtract the x-coordinates: 8 − 1 = 7.

Answer: 7 units

Real-world graphs

Data from a table can be graphed as points. Each row of the table becomes one ordered pair. The axis titles tell what each number means.

Hours worked (x)1234
Dollars earned (y)8162432
Example

If the pattern continues, what point comes after (4, 32)?

The hours go up by 1 and the dollars go up by 8: (4 + 1, 32 + 8).

Answer: (5, 40)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Switching the numbers: plotting (3, 7) at right 7, up 3Go right first (x), then up (y)
Counting the first grid line as 1The origin is 0. Count the spaces from it
Thinking (0, 5) is on the x-axisx = 0 means no move right, so it is on the y-axis
Counting dots to find a distanceSubtract the coordinates that change
Ignoring the scale on a real-world graphCheck what each axis counts by

faq.q: How do you find the coordinates of a point?
faq.a: Start at the origin. Count how far right the point is (the x-coordinate), then how far up (the y-coordinate), and write them as (x, y).

faq.q: Which comes first in an ordered pair, x or y?
faq.a: The x-coordinate always comes first. A helpful rule is “across, then up”: (4, 7) means right 4, up 7.

faq.q: What is the origin on a coordinate plane?
faq.a: The origin is the point where the x-axis and the y-axis cross. Its coordinates are (0, 0), and every point is found by starting there.
It is the top-right part of the coordinate plane, where both coordinates are 0 or greater. In Grade 5, students graph points only in the first quadrant.

sets.title: Read the coordinates of a point

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 3, then up 5. Point A is at (3, 5). The x-coordinate (across) always comes first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 6, then up 2. Point B is at (6, 2). The x-coordinate (across) always comes first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point C?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 2, then up 7. Point C is at (2, 7). The x-coordinate (across) always comes first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point P?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 8, then up 3. Point P is at (8, 3). The x-coordinate (across) always comes first. (3, 8) is point Q: the numbers are switched.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point F?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 1, then up 4. Point F is at (1, 4). The x-coordinate (across) always comes first. (4, 1) is point E: the numbers are switched.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point G?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 7, then up 6. Point G is at (7, 6). The x-coordinate (across) always comes first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point H?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 5, then up 9. Point H is at (5, 9). The x-coordinate (across) always comes first. (9, 5) is point J: the numbers are switched.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point K?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 1, then up 3. Point K is at (1, 3). The x-coordinate (across) always comes first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point M?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 9, then up 7. Point M is at (9, 7). The x-coordinate (across) always comes first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point R?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 6, then up 8. Point R is at (6, 8). The x-coordinate (across) always comes first.

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point S?
items.e: The x-coordinate tells how far to go across. Point S is 7 units to the right of the origin, so x = 7. (4 is its y-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the y-coordinate of point T?
items.e: The y-coordinate tells how far to go up. Point T is 6 units up from the x-axis, so y = 6. (3 is its x-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point U?
items.e: Point U is 5 units to the right of the origin, so its x-coordinate is 5. Point V is the one at (2, 5).

items.q: What is the y-coordinate of point W?
items.e: Point W is 5 units up, so its y-coordinate is 5. Its x-coordinate is 8: W is at (8, 5).

items.q: In an ordered pair, which coordinate comes first?
items.e: An ordered pair is always written (x, y). The x-coordinate (how far across) comes first, then the y-coordinate (how far up).

items.q: Which axis goes across, from left to right?
items.e: The x-axis goes across. The y-axis goes up. They meet at the origin, (0, 0).

items.q: In the ordered pair (6, 2), what does the 6 tell you?
items.e: The first number is the x-coordinate. It tells how far to go right from the origin: right 6.

items.q: In the ordered pair (6, 2), what does the 2 tell you?
items.e: The second number is the y-coordinate. It tells how far to go up: up 2.

items.q: Owen starts at the origin. He goes right 4, then up 9. Which ordered pair names his point?
items.e: Right 4 gives x = 4, and up 9 gives y = 9. Write x first: (4, 9).

items.q: To plot the point (5, 3), what do you do first from the origin?
items.e: The first number, 5, is the x-coordinate. Go right 5 along the x-axis first, then up 3.

sets.title: Find the point for an ordered pair

items.q: Which point is at (3, 7)?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 3, then up 7: that is point D. Point A is at (7, 3): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (5, 2)?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 5, then up 2: that is point B. Point A is at (2, 5): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (1, 6)?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 1, then up 6: that is point A. Point B is at (6, 1): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (8, 4)?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 8, then up 4: that is point C. Point A is at (4, 8): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (4, 9)?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 4, then up 9: that is point A. Point B is at (9, 4): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (6, 3)?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 6, then up 3: that is point B. Point A is at (3, 6): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (2, 5)?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 2, then up 5: that is point C. Point A is at (5, 2): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (7, 1)?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 7, then up 1: that is point D. Point A is at (1, 7): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (9, 6)?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 9, then up 6: that is point A. Point B is at (6, 9): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (2, 8)?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 2, then up 8: that is point B. Point A is at (8, 2): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point has an x-coordinate of 5?
items.e: The x-coordinate is the first number: how far across. Point C is 5 units to the right, at (5, 2). The point at (2, 5) has a y-coordinate of 5, not an x-coordinate of 5.

items.q: Which point has a y-coordinate of 3?
items.e: The y-coordinate is the second number: how far up. Point D is 3 units up, at (6, 3). The point at (3, 6) has an x-coordinate of 3.

items.q: Noah says point B is at (6, 3). What mistake did he make?
items.e: Point B is 3 units right and 6 units up, so it is at (3, 6). Noah wrote the up number first.

items.q: Maya says point E is at (5, 3). What mistake did she make?
items.e: Point E is at (4, 2). Maya counted the first grid line as 1, so both numbers came out 1 too big. Count the spaces from the origin, which is 0.

items.q: Are (2, 5) and (5, 2) the same point?
c: Yes, they use the same numbers
items.e: (2, 5) is right 2, up 5. (5, 2) is right 5, up 2. The order of the numbers changes where the point is.

items.q: Kai wants to plot (7, 1). He goes up 7, then right 1. Which point did he plot by mistake?
items.e: Going right 1 and up 7 lands on (1, 7). To plot (7, 1), go right 7 first, then up 1.

items.q: Which point is farther to the right: (2, 9) or (6, 1)?
items.e: How far right a point is depends on the x-coordinate, the first number. 6 is more than 2, so (6, 1) is farther right.

items.q: Which point is higher on the grid: (8, 3) or (2, 5)?
items.e: How high a point is depends on the y-coordinate, the second number. 5 is more than 3, so (2, 5) is higher.

items.q: Which point is straight above (4, 2)?
items.e: Points straight above each other have the same x-coordinate. (4, 6) has x = 4, the same as (4, 2), and a bigger y.

items.q: Which point is straight to the right of (1, 5)?
items.e: Points straight across from each other have the same y-coordinate. (7, 5) has y = 5, the same as (1, 5), and a bigger x.

sets.title: Points on the axes and the origin

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Point A is on the y-axis, so it did not move right at all: x = 0. Go up 5: (0, 5).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Point B is on the x-axis. Go right 6 and up 0: (6, 0). A point on the x-axis always has y = 0.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point M?
items.e: Point M is at the origin, where the axes meet. It is 0 right and 0 up: (0, 0).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point K?
items.e: Point K is on the y-axis, 8 units up. Its x-coordinate is 0: (0, 8). (8, 0) would be on the x-axis.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point R?
items.e: Point R is on the x-axis, 9 units right. It does not go up, so y = 0: (9, 0).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point T?
items.e: Point T is on the y-axis, 2 units up: (0, 2). Point S is at (2, 0), on the x-axis.

items.q: Where is the point (0, 7)?
items.e: x = 0 means the point does not move right. It goes straight up the y-axis to 7.

items.q: Where is the point (6, 0)?
items.e: y = 0 means the point does not move up. It stays on the x-axis at 6.

items.q: Where is the point (0, 0)?
items.e: Both coordinates are 0, so the point does not move at all. It is the origin.

items.q: Where is the point (3, 3)?
items.e: Neither coordinate is 0, so the point is inside the grid: right 3 and up 3.

items.q: Which point is on the y-axis?
items.e: Point A is at (0, 4). Its x-coordinate is 0, so it sits on the y-axis. The point at (4, 0) is on the x-axis, and the point at (1, 3) is 1 unit to the right of the y-axis.

items.q: Which point is on the x-axis?
items.e: Point D is at (5, 0). Its y-coordinate is 0, so it sits on the x-axis. The point at (0, 5) is on the y-axis, and the point at (4, 1) is 1 unit above the x-axis.

items.q: Which point is on the x-axis?
items.e: Points on the x-axis do not go up, so their y-coordinate (the second number) is 0: (4, 0).

items.q: Which point is on the y-axis?
items.e: Points on the y-axis do not go right, so their x-coordinate (the first number) is 0: (0, 9).

items.q: Every point on the x-axis has the same y-coordinate. What is it?
items.e: Points on the x-axis do not go up at all, so y = 0. Examples: (3, 0), (7, 0).

items.q: Every point on the y-axis has the same x-coordinate. What is it?
items.e: Points on the y-axis do not go right at all, so x = 0. Examples: (0, 2), (0, 8).

items.q: What are the coordinates of the origin?
items.e: The origin is where the axes meet. It is the 0 on both number lines, so it is (0, 0).

items.q: What is the point where the x-axis and the y-axis meet called?
items.e: The axes meet at the origin, (0, 0). Every point is found by starting there.

items.q: Grace says (0, 5) is on the x-axis because it has a 0 first. Is she right?
c: No, it is on the y-axis
No, it is at the origin
Yes, every 0 is on the x-axis
items.e: x = 0 means the point does not move right, so it stays on the y-axis and goes up 5. Points on the x-axis have y = 0.

items.q: A point starts at the origin and moves up 4. What are its coordinates now?
items.e: It did not move right, so x = 0. It moved up 4, so y = 4: (0, 4), on the y-axis.

sets.title: Distance, moves and shapes on the grid

items.q: How many units long is line segment AB?
items.e: Both points have x = 2, so they are on the same up-and-down line. Subtract the y-coordinates: 8 − 3 = 5 units. Count spaces, not dots.

items.q: How many units long is line segment AB?
items.e: Both points have y = 4, so they are on the same across line. Subtract the x-coordinates: 7 − 1 = 6 units. Count spaces, not dots.

items.q: How many units long is line segment MN?
items.e: Both points have x = 6, so they are on the same up-and-down line. Subtract the y-coordinates: 9 − 1 = 8 units. Count spaces, not dots.

items.q: How many units long is line segment CD?
items.e: Both points have y = 5, so they are on the same across line. Subtract the x-coordinates: 9 − 2 = 7 units. Count spaces, not dots.

items.q: How many units is it from (3, 2) to (3, 10)?
items.e: Both points have x = 3, so they are on the same up-and-down line. Subtract the y-coordinates: 10 − 2 = 8 units. Count spaces, not dots.

items.q: A line segment goes from (1, 6) to (8, 6). How long is it?
items.e: Both points have y = 6, so they are on the same across line. Subtract the x-coordinates: 8 − 1 = 7 units. Count spaces, not dots.

items.q: Nora finds the distance from (5, 2) to (5, 9). She counts the dots on the grid line and gets 8. What is the real distance?
items.e: Distance is the number of spaces between the points: 9 − 2 = 7. Counting dots counts the starting point too, so it gives 1 too many.

items.q: Point A is at (3, 4). It moves 2 units to the right. Where is it now?
items.e: Moving right changes only x: 3 + 2 = 5. The y-coordinate stays 4: (5, 4).

items.q: Point B is at (6, 2). It moves 5 units up. Where is it now?
items.e: Moving up changes only y: 2 + 5 = 7. The x-coordinate stays 6: (6, 7).

items.q: Point C is at (2, 5). It moves 4 units right and 3 units down. Where is it now?
items.e: Right 4 changes x: 2 + 4 = 6. Down 3 changes y: 5 − 3 = 2. The new point is (6, 2).

items.q: Point A is at (4, 7). Point B is 3 units straight to the left of A. What are the coordinates of B?
items.e: Left means x gets smaller: 4 − 3 = 1. Straight left means y stays 7: (1, 7).

items.q: Which point is 4 units to the right of point P?
items.e: Point D is at (6, 3): x grows by 4 (2 + 4 = 6) and y stays 3. The point at (2, 7) is 4 units up, not right.

items.q: Which point is 3 units below point P?
items.e: Point B is at (5, 3): y gets smaller by 3 (6 − 3 = 3) and x stays 5. The point at (5, 9) is 3 units above, and (5, 2) is 4 units below.

items.q: A, B and C are 3 corners of a rectangle. What are the coordinates of the 4th corner, D?
items.e: D is in line with A up and down, so x = 1. It is in line with C across, so y = 5. D is at (1, 5).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 corners of a rectangle. What are the coordinates of the 4th corner, D?
items.e: D is in line with C up and down, so x = 5. It is in line with A across, so y = 1. D is at (5, 1).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 corners of a square. What are the coordinates of the 4th corner, D?
items.e: D is in line with A up and down, so x = 3. It is in line with C across, so y = 6. D is at (3, 6).

items.q: A rectangle has corners at (1, 1), (6, 1), (6, 4) and (1, 4). What is its perimeter in units?
items.e: The bottom side goes from x = 1 to x = 6: 5 units. The left side goes from y = 1 to y = 4: 3 units. Perimeter = 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 units.

items.q: A rectangle has corners at (2, 1), (7, 1), (7, 5) and (2, 5). What is its area in square units?
items.e: The length is 7 − 2 = 5 units and the width is 5 − 1 = 4 units. Area = 5 × 4 = 20 square units.

items.q: Which point is on the same up-and-down line as (3, 5)?
items.e: Points on the same up-and-down line have the same x-coordinate. (3, 1) has x = 3. (1, 5) is on the same across line instead.

items.q: Ben walks only along grid lines from A to B. What is the shortest number of units he can walk?
items.e: A is at (1, 2) and B is at (6, 6). Go right 6 − 1 = 5 units and up 6 − 2 = 4 units. 5 + 4 = 9 units.

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, B = bench. What are the coordinates of the pond?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 7, then up 7. The pond is at (7, 7).

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, B = bench. Which place is at (7, 2)?
items.e: Go right 7, then up 2: that is B, the bench. The slide is at (2, 7): the numbers are switched.

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, B = bench. Ruby walks from the gate straight up to the fountain. How many units does she walk?
items.e: The gate is at (4, 0) and the fountain is at (4, 4). Same x, so subtract the y-coordinates: 4 − 0 = 4 units.

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, B = bench. How many units is it from the slide straight across to the pond?
items.e: The slide is at (2, 7) and the pond is at (7, 7). Same y, so subtract the x-coordinates: 7 − 2 = 5 units.

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, B = bench. A picnic table will go 3 units to the right of the fountain. Where will it be?
items.e: The fountain is at (4, 4). Right 3 changes only x: 4 + 3 = 7. The table will be at (7, 4).

items.q: The map shows where Luis lives. H = home, S = school, L = library, C = café. Each unit is 1 block. What are the coordinates of the library?
items.e: Start at the origin. Go right 9, then up 6. The library is at (9, 6).

items.q: The map shows where Luis lives. H = home, S = school, L = library, C = café. Each unit is 1 block. Luis walks from home straight up to school. How many blocks does he walk?
items.e: Home is at (3, 1) and school is at (3, 6). Same x, so subtract: 6 − 1 = 5 blocks.

items.q: The map shows where Luis lives. H = home, S = school, L = library, C = café. Each unit is 1 block. After school, he walks straight across to the library. How many blocks is that?
items.e: School is at (3, 6) and the library is at (9, 6). Same y, so subtract: 9 − 3 = 6 blocks.

items.q: The map shows where Luis lives. H = home, S = school, L = library, C = café. Each unit is 1 block. Luis walks from home to the library along the streets (the grid lines). What is the shortest number of blocks?
items.e: Home is at (3, 1) and the library is at (9, 6). Go right 9 − 3 = 6 blocks and up 6 − 1 = 5 blocks. 6 + 5 = 11 blocks.

items.q: Sofia earns the same amount for each hour she works. The graph shows (hours worked, dollars earned). What does the point (3, 24) mean?
items.e: The first number is on the x-axis: hours worked. The second number is on the y-axis: dollars earned. So in 3 hours she earns $24.

items.q: Sofia earns the same amount for each hour she works. The graph shows (hours worked, dollars earned). How much does she earn in 2 hours?
items.e: Find 2 on the x-axis and go up to the point. It is at 16 on the y-axis, which counts by 8: $16. (2 is the hours, not the dollars.)

items.q: Sofia earns the same amount for each hour she works. The graph shows (hours worked, dollars earned). How much does she earn for each hour?
items.e: The point (1, 8) shows $8 for 1 hour. Each hour adds $8: 8, 16, 24, 32.

items.q: Sofia earns the same amount for each hour she works. The graph shows (hours worked, dollars earned). If the pattern continues, which point comes next?
items.e: The hours go up by 1 and the dollars go up by 8. After (4, 32) comes (4 + 1, 32 + 8) = (5, 40).

items.q: Sofia earns the same amount for each hour she works. The graph shows (hours worked, dollars earned). Working 0 hours earns $0. Which point shows this?
items.e: 0 hours is x = 0 and $0 is y = 0. That point is the origin, (0, 0).

items.q: The graph shows the height of a plant each week, as (week, height in cm). What does the point (0, 2) mean?
c: After 2 weeks, the plant was 0 cm tall.
The plant grew 2 cm each week.
At the start, the plant was 2 cm tall.
items.e: Week 0 is the start. The y-coordinate, 2, is the height. So the plant was 2 cm tall when the graph started.

items.q: The graph shows the height of a plant each week, as (week, height in cm). How tall was the plant at week 3?
items.e: Find 3 on the x-axis and go up to the point. It is at 8 on the y-axis, which counts by 2: 8 cm.

items.q: The graph shows the height of a plant each week, as (week, height in cm). How many centimeters does the plant grow each week?
items.e: Each week the point is 1 grid space higher. On this y-axis 1 space is 2 cm, so the plant grows 2 cm: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

items.q: The graph shows the height of a plant each week, as (week, height in cm). If the pattern continues, which point shows week 5?
items.e: Each week the height goes up 2 cm. At week 4 it is 10 cm, so at week 5 it is 12 cm: (5, 12). The week comes first.

items.q: Eli reads 15 pages each day. His table shows the total pages read so far: Day 1: 15, Day 2: 30, Day 3: 45. He plots each row as (day, pages). Which point does he plot for Day 2?
items.e: The day comes first and the pages come second. Day 2 has 30 pages: (2, 30).

items.q: Tickets cost $4 each. Ava graphs (number of tickets, total cost). Which point is on her graph?
items.e: 3 tickets cost 3 × 4 = $12, so the point is (3, 12). The number of tickets comes first. (4 tickets would cost $16.)
